messages.author: d7748fae4a649ddf
messages.subject: Overestimation of copy number
parts:
Dear Gavin,

I have recently started using TitanCNA for some noisy data. It seems to consistently over-estimate the copy number especially in regions where there is no change. So most commonly I see a copy number estimation of 3 where it should have been 2. ichorCNA however predicts the copy number correctly in those regions. So I think this might be because most of the noise is in the BAF data and the readCount data is fairly alright. 

I was just wondering if there is  way to adjust for this? For instance if there is a parameter that increases the importance of ReadCounts over BAF? Or any other parameter that might be of any help for analysing noisy data?

Thanks a lot. 
Best
Mo

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: Overestimation of copy number
parts:
Hi Mo,

Thank you for your interest in TITAN. 

Without seeing some example plots of the data, it is hard for me to know is going on exactly.  However, there are a few ways, in general, to help prevent over-segmentation.  
- Increase txnExpLen: This value is used to govern the transition probabilities. The higher this value is set, fewer segments will be generated.
- Increase minDepth: This value is used to help filter which SNPs are used for BAF. If your data is noisy, then it might be a coverage issue. This argument can help with that.
- Increase alphaK: This value is the hyper parameter for the Gaussian model (log ratio). If your data is very clean, then increasing this value will allow for better fitting of the model and also increase the probabilities contributed by the log ratio compared to the allelic ratio. This parameter change will likely give you the biggest improvement if the log ratio data is really clean.

You make a good point about weighting read coverage and allelic fraction (BAF) more directly. I have considered adding this into the model but never got around to it.

Hope this helps,

Gavin

messages.subject: Re: Overestimation of copy number
parts:
Dear Gavin,

Thank you very much for your reply. I have already tried some of these parameters with not much luck. Attached you can see an example.

On the left is my control data with default parameters which returns very clean profiles. On the right is the corresponding noisy data. On the top right as you can see, despite the noise, ichorCNA correctly predicts the copy numbers, however when the data is passed on to Titan, it predicts too many segments. When I increase the txnExpLen parameter to 1e20 to reduce the segment numbers however, it decides to estimate a higher ploidy for the 6q segment. Any idea why this might be happening and if there might be a way to solve it?

Thanks again
Best
Mo

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: Overestimation of copy number
parts:
Hi Mo,

Perhaps another way to account for noisy data is actually to decrease the alphaK argument from 10000 to 5000 or 1000. This is the hyper parameter for the variance parameter, which in term is used to model the variability of the log ratio data. Earlier, I had thought you said you had clean log ratios.  While the log ratio is cleaner than the BAF, it isn't as clean as your control sample.

See if this helps.

Best,
Gavin
